title: Fast Fiction Factory High-Fidelity Raster Pilot

shots.review_intent: 匿名の制度空間を、人間の身体性と建築的な奥行きで検証する。
shots.alt_ja: 半透明の仕切り越しに、会議室で話し合う匿名の人々を捉えた写実的な室内写真
shots.truth_boundary: 有罪の演技、個人特定、単純な悪役化を避ける。

generation_record.tool: OpenAI built-in image_gen tool (default built-in mode)
generation_record.postprocess_recipe: Sharp center crop and resize from observed 1672x941 PNG to 1600x900 JPEG; quality 94; 4:4:4 chroma; mozjpeg; no vector or procedural scene content introduced.
generation_record.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: 16:9 cinematic review still for Fast Fiction Factory shot-b04-01
Primary request: a plausible anonymous institutional council interior seen through a partially frosted glass partition, with a small group of unidentifiable adults seated or standing in restrained discussion
Scene/backdrop: contemporary but timeless public-institution meeting room, real architectural depth, layered glass, wood, muted stone, subtle atmospheric perspective
Subject: 4 to 6 anonymous adults with anatomically plausible human proportions, natural posture, varied body shapes, faces obscured by distance, angle, and frosted glass; no identifiable official
Style/medium: high-fidelity cinematic editorial photography, realistic materials and human anatomy, subtle film grain
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape, spatial depth from foreground partition to midground people to background architecture, suitable for a very slow push-in
Lighting/mood: neutral cool daylight with restrained tension; neither ominous nor celebratory; no villain lighting
Color palette: muted slate, soft gray, aged brass accents, natural skin and fabric tones
Materials/textures: convincing frosted glass, wood grain, worn fabric, stone, realistic skin and hair silhouettes
Constraints: no embedded text, no Japanese text, no logos, no watermark, no recognizable public figure, no weapons, no dramatic confrontation
Avoid: vector art, SVG look, flat illustration, CSS shapes, Canvas primitives, rounded bottle or pawn silhouettes, generic geometric people, repeated circles or rectangles, diagram UI, dashboard cards, near-blank abstraction, theatrical villain lighting
Output intent: one materially convincing raster scene that is unmistakably different from geometric silhouette pseudo-art and preserves the truth boundary that guilt, identity, and motive are unconfirmed

non_match_evidence: five anatomically plausible seated or standing adults with varied human posture
foreground glass, midground people, and background architecture establish spatial depth
photographic skin, hair, fabric, glass, wood, and stone texture
no rounded bottle or pawn-body construction
no identifiable official and no villain-lighting cue

generation_record.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: 16:9 cinematic review still for Fast Fiction Factory shot-b05-02
Primary request: a materially convincing brass moth-shaped mechanical object resting on a dark archival worktable, its possible purpose deliberately unresolved
Scene/backdrop: quiet conservation or research workbench with shallow depth of field, aged paper and indistinct precision tools present only as atmospheric context
Subject: one intricate brass moth or moth-shaped mechanism with believable metal construction, articulated engraved wings, small screws, oxidation, scratches, and hand-worked edges; it remains inert and closed
Style/medium: high-fidelity cinematic macro photography, practical prop realism, photographic texture
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape, the moth materially dominates the frame off-center, with three very subtle and visually different evidence zones in the background that can support separate HTML candidate labels later; no cards or panels
Lighting/mood: restrained warm side light and cool ambient fill, investigative but not supernatural
Color palette: aged brass, umber paper, charcoal textile, muted steel
Materials/textures: patinated brass, fine engraving, worn paper fibers, dusty glass, soft cloth
Constraints: no embedded text, no Japanese text, no labels in the image, no logo, no watermark; moth is static; no glow, no flight, no open hatch, no keyhole, no surveillance lens, no projected image, no indicated correct function
Avoid: vector art, SVG look, line-art moth, enlarged icon, flat illustration, CSS shapes, Canvas primitives, generic geometry, central circle motif, three identical dashboard cards, repeated panels, diagram arrows, UI, near-blank abstraction
Output intent: one materially plausible raster object image, unmistakably different from the rejected generic line-icon moth and repeated UI-card composition, while preserving unresolved candidate functions

non_match_evidence: engraved brass thickness, screws, patina, scratches, and assembly seams establish a material object
archival paper, cloth, glass, and metal tools form a photographic environment

generation_record.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: 16:9 cinematic review still for Fast Fiction Factory shot-b02-03
Primary request: an extreme close-up of a plausible antique brass clock or pocket-watch face clearly displaying 9:17, with a small brass moth object or its physically plausible reflection appearing near the lower edge
Scene/backdrop: dark archival desk or repair bench, shallow depth of field, background fully photographic and materially grounded
Subject: aged mechanical clock face with real glass, engraved metal bezel, worn enamel dial, minute hand pointing to 17 minutes slightly past the 3, hour hand slightly past 9; a small materially convincing brass moth rests beside the bezel or is reflected in the curved glass
Style/medium: high-fidelity cinematic macro photography, practical prop realism
Composition/framing: wide 16:9 landscape, extreme close-up, clock face dominates the frame and may extend beyond its edges; moth is a secondary material motif; suitable for controlled parallax
Lighting/mood: restrained warm brass highlights with cool shadow fill, investigative and quiet, no supernatural glow
Color palette: aged ivory enamel, tarnished brass, charcoal, muted blue-gray
Materials/textures: scratched glass, patinated brass, fine dust, engraved numerals, real metal hands and pivots
Constraints: the hands must visibly read 9:17; no embedded Japanese text, no extra labels, no logos, no watermark; the scene does not prove the clock stopped and does not establish causality between clock and moth
Avoid: flat vector dial, SVG look, illustration, CSS shapes, Canvas primitives, diagram rings or arrows, generic icons, UI, repeated geometric panels, near-blank abstraction, magical glow, broken-clock implication, cause-and-effect symbolism
Output intent: one materially plausible raster clock image unmistakably different from a flat vector clock face, preserving 9:17 as a motif rather than a confirmed stopped time

non_match_evidence: enamel wear, scratched glass, engraved bezel, dust, and metal hands establish a physical clock
the long hand points slightly past three and the short hand points at nine, reading approximately 9:17
the moth is a separate brass object beside the bezel
no diagrammatic rings, arrows, UI, or flat vector dial
no visual effect asserts that the clock stopped or that the moth caused it
